extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: A benchmark comprising 20,000 conflicts, evenly distributed between language and vision paradigms, designed to evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to detect self-contradictory instructions.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, and Dequan Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is constructed using an automatic dataset creation framework called AutoCreate, which uses a small batch of manually input seeds to automatically generate data via Large Language Models (LLMs) through a Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner loop.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset is primarily generated by LLMs, with the SemanticConflict task specifically utilizing external data from the ImageNet dataset.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data is manipulated by introducing conflicts into generated text or images. For example, in V-L conflicts, image captions are modified, numerical data in charts is altered, or correct labels in questions are substituted with similar but different objects.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A Cleaner module removes data that does not meet quality standards during the generation loop.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts and LLMs double-check the quality of the generated dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Evaluation consistency between human experts and LLM agents was measured using Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically GPT-4, were used as evaluation agents and for data generation.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark provides a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction, promoting inclusivity, and fostering trust and reliability in AI systems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms, lacks fine-grained control to determine the conflict degree, and does not provide a detailed study on the attention mechanism of LMMs.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to detect and comprehend conflicting instructions.
